description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the number of child nodes (tree width) and the accuracy percentage (Accuracy@1) for two different language models, GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet, in the context of Visual Navigation and geometry problems (Geomverse). The x-axis is labeled "Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width)" and is a linear scale ranging from 1 to 7. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy@1 (%)" and is a linear scale ranging from 15 to 35. The plot shows two lines: the solid blue line represents GPT-4o, and the dashed blue line with 'x' markers represents Claude-3.5-Sonnet. For GPT-4o, the accuracy starts at 24.4% with 1 child node, increases to 28.9% with 3 child nodes, peaks at 34.4% with 5 child nodes, and then decreases to 31.1% with 7 child nodes. For Claude-3.5-Sonnet, the accuracy starts at 26.7% with 1 child node, increases to 27.8% with 3 child nodes, decreases to 24.4% with 5 child nodes, and further decreases to 20.0% with 7 child nodes. The plot indicates that both models show an inverted U-shaped trend with respect to tree width, with GPT-4o generally outperforming Claude-3.5-Sonnet across the range of child nodes.
